# firstboot_app (Resource)

A container app: an image or a git repository, run and routed for you.

Two ways to start one, and they are exclusive. Give an `image` to run something that is already built; give a `source_url` to have the platform build the repository, in which case the first build is queued with the app and this resource waits for it.

**Starting and stopping an app is not modelled here.** It is an action rather than a property, the same way a server's power state is: a plan should not decide to stop something that is serving traffic.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter. Renaming is applied in place; the `code` and the default hostname do not follow it.
- `plan` (String) App plan slug. It decides the memory and CPU limits, the monthly price and the replica ceiling. Changed in place, which restarts the containers.

### Optional

- `auto_deploy` (Boolean) Whether a push to the tracked branch builds and deploys by itself.

Leaving it ON means the running image can change without Terraform, which is usually the point of connecting a repository. It is switched off automatically when the source is unlinked.
- `build_command` (String) Overrides the preset's build step.
- `builder` (String) Who writes the Dockerfile. `dockerfile` (the default) means the repository carries one; `preset` means the platform generates one for the stack named in `preset`, which is how a repository with no Dockerfile deploys.
- `context_dir` (String) Repository subdirectory to build from, for a monorepo. Relative, no leading slash.
- `dockerfile_path` (String) Dockerfile path relative to the build directory. Defaults to `Dockerfile`, and only applies to the `dockerfile` builder.
- `env` (Block List) Environment variables. The whole set is replaced on every change: a variable absent here is removed.

**They are never read back.** The endpoint that returns decrypted values writes an audit entry on every call, so refreshing them on each plan would fill the account's audit log with reads nobody made deliberately. The consequence is honest and worth knowing: a value changed in the panel is NOT detected as drift, and the next apply that touches anything else will overwrite it with whatever the configuration says. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--env))
- `git_connection_id` (String) A connection from the account's git integrations, for a PRIVATE repository. Every build then mints a short-lived credential from it. Omit it for a public repository.
- `git_ref` (String) Branch or tag to build. Defaults to `main`.
- `health_path` (String) An HTTP path a new version has to answer before it takes over traffic. Empty means a plain TCP check on the app's port, which proves the process is listening and nothing about whether it works.
- `image` (String) An OCI image from an allowed public registry. Leave it out when `source_url` is set: the build produces the image, and this then reports whichever image the app is running.
- `install_command` (String) Overrides the preset's dependency install step.
- `output_dir` (String) The directory that matters at the end of the build: the document root for `php`, the build output for `static`. Empty means the preset's default.
- `port` (Number) The port the app listens on inside the container. Defaults to 8080.
- `preset` (String) Stack slug for the `preset` builder. Required with it, refused without it.
- `project_id` (String) Optional project to group the app under. Changing it moves the app in place; it is not a replacement.
- `region` (String) Region slug; defaults to the first active region when omitted. There is no migration between regions, so a change replaces the app.

**Write-only.** An app's body does not report which region it landed in, so this is never refreshed and drift in it cannot be detected. It is not marked Computed for exactly that reason: a computed value nobody can fill would stay unknown.
- `replicas_max` (Number) The most the platform may run, bounded by the plan. Equal to the minimum pins the count.
- `replicas_min` (Number) The fewest containers to keep running.
- `runtime` (String) Isolation runtime: `runc`, `runsc` (gVisor) or `kata` (microVM). The last two need a node that registers them, so asking for one where none exists is refused rather than downgraded.

Chosen when the container is placed and not changeable afterwards.
- `source_url` (String) An HTTPS git repository to build. Removing it UNLINKS the app: it keeps running its current image and auto-deploy is switched off with the link.
- `start_command` (String) Overrides the image's own command, run through a shell. Leave it out unless detection picked the wrong process.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags on this app, used to select it from a `firstboot_*` data source and to filter it in the panel.

At most 10, each up to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit. `env:prod` is a convention, not a schema: a tag is one flat string.

**Written exactly as given.** The API stores tags lowercased, so a tag that is not already lowercase is refused at plan time rather than silently rewritten — a rewritten value would differ from the configuration on every subsequent plan.
- `wait_for_build` (Boolean) Whether apply waits for a build it started to finish. With it off, an apply that changes the source succeeds while the build is still running and can still fail -- the app then keeps serving its previous image and the plan reported nothing.

### Read-Only

- `code` (String)
- `created_at` (String)
- `desired_state` (String) What the platform is trying to run: `running`, `stopped` or `suspended`. Changed through the panel's start and stop, not from here.
- `id` (String) The app's short code, which is also its identity everywhere else in the API and the label in its default hostname.
- `observed_state` (String) What the node last reported. It lags `desired_state` while a deploy is rolling, and the gap between the two is what a deploy actually is.
- `replicas_desired` (Number) How many containers the platform currently wants to run.
- `url` (String) The default hostname the app is served on.

<a id="nestedblock--env"></a>
### Nested Schema for `env`

Required:

- `key` (String) A shell-exportable name: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The value. It is sealed at rest on the platform and it is written to the TERRAFORM STATE FILE in the clear, like every other attribute -- protect the state file accordingly.

Optional:

- `phase` (String) `run` (the default), `build`, or `both`. A `build` value becomes an argument of the build command and is echoed into the build log, which is why it is bounded and why it cannot also be secret.
- `secret` (Boolean) Masks the value in the panel and omits it from exports.

**Not an encryption boundary.** The node receives every value in the clear, because a container cannot start otherwise. Refused together with a `build` phase.
